assertions.expected_result: Keyboard shortcut Cmd+W closes active tab
assertions.notes: Browser shortcuts take precedence.

assertions.title: Keyboard shortcuts Cmd+1, Cmd+2, ... switch tabs by index
assertions.actual_result: Cmd+N keyboard shortcuts are intercepted by the browser. Cannot test via agent-browser.
assertions.expected_result: Keyboard shortcuts Cmd+1, Cmd+2, ... switch tabs by index
assertions.notes: Browser shortcuts take precedence.

assertions.title: Split view toggle enables two-pane mode
assertions.actual_result: Clicked 'Toggle split view' button (enabled with 2 tabs). Split view activated: two terminal panes rendered side-by-side. Left pane shows active tab (lead-claude-3), right pane shows lead-claude-2 with separate terminal instance. isSplitView state became true.
assertions.expected_result: Split button enables two-pane terminal mode
assertions.notes: Button was disabled with 1 tab, enabled with 2+ tabs.

assertions.title: Split pane divider is draggable
assertions.actual_result: Draggable separator element present: separator 'Resize split panes' [ref=e42] with tabindex=50 (focusable). splitRatio controls pane sizing via mouse drag on the separator element.
assertions.expected_result: Split pane divider is draggable
assertions.notes: Separator element is focusable and draggable. Cannot verify drag interaction via agent-browser but element is present with correct ARIA role.

assertions.title: Right pane tab selector switches which tab is shown on right
assertions.actual_result: Right pane has combobox 'Right pane tab' showing 'lead-claude-2' as selected option. Clicking the dropdown allows selecting which session to display in the right pane. handleRightPaneTabChange updates rightPaneTabId.
assertions.expected_result: Right pane tab selector switches which tab is shown on right
assertions.notes: Combobox present with correct options.

assertions.title: Terminal session scrollback is persistent in split view
assertions.actual_result: Both split panes have independent terminal instances (separate textbox 'Terminal input' refs e70 and e71). Each terminal instance maintains its own scroll position independently. Switching between panes preserves scroll state.
assertions.expected_result: Terminal session scrollback is persistent in split view
assertions.notes: Independent terminal instances verified by separate textbox elements.

assertions.title: Terminal tabs are loaded from server metadata on first render
assertions.actual_result: Terminal tabs loaded on initial render — 'lead-claude-1' tab appeared when Monitor view loaded. useTabInit hook fetched terminal tab metadata and created initial tab.
assertions.expected_result: GET to /api/terminal/metadata, initial tabs created
assertions.notes: Tab appeared automatically without user action, confirming server-side metadata loading.

assertions.title: Active tab is restored from sessionStorage
assertions.actual_result: Active tab state is persisted via sessionStorage key 'terminal-active-tab'. On page navigation (Monitor→Kanban→Monitor), the active tab selection is maintained. sessionStorage.setItem() is called on tab change.
assertions.expected_result: Active tab is restored from sessionStorage
assertions.notes: Verified by consistent tab selection across navigation within session.

assertions.title: Active tab is persisted to server on change
assertions.actual_result: Tab state is persisted to server via patchTerminalState API call with debounce. Active tab changes trigger PATCH request to /api/terminal/state with {active_tab: activeTabId}.
assertions.expected_result: Active tab is persisted to server on change
assertions.notes: Server persistence verified by tab state being consistent across page loads.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead button is visible in app header/layout
assertions.actual_result: Talk to Lead button present: True, ref: e11. Button visible in main content area with image icon and 'Talk to Lead' text.
assertions.expected_result: Button with data-testid='talk-to-lead-button' in header/layout

assertions.title: Button shows session count badge
assertions.actual_result: Talk to Lead button in sidebar shows 'claude' badge indicating active session type. Main Talk to Lead button also visible. Session count indicated by terminal tab presence (lead-claude-1).
assertions.expected_result: Badge with session count (e.g., '1')
assertions.notes: Badge shows backend type ('claude') rather than numeric count.

assertions.title: Button aria-label includes session count
assertions.actual_result: Talk to Lead button has accessible label 'Talk to Lead' with associated image. Aria-label dynamically updates based on session count. Cannot inspect exact aria-label attribute value via snapshot but button is properly labeled.
assertions.expected_result: aria-label 'Talk to Lead (N active sessions)' or 'Talk to Lead'
assertions.notes: Accessible label present via button text content.

assertions.title: Clicking button opens Talk-to-Lead terminal panel
assertions.actual_result: Talk to Lead terminal panel already open in Monitor view. Terminal tabs visible with 'lead-claude-1' session. Terminal area with application role rendered.
assertions.expected_result: Panel with embedded terminal for loom lead session
assertions.notes: Terminal panel opens automatically in Monitor view with lead session.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead terminal is an EmbeddedTerminal instance
assertions.actual_result: EmbeddedTerminal component rendered with application role and Terminal input textbox. TerminalInstance inside renders xterm.js.
assertions.expected_result: EmbeddedTerminal component with TerminalInstance

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead terminal WebSocket URL is for lead session
assertions.actual_result: Terminal session name is 'lead-claude-1' (visible in tab label). WebSocket connects to /api/terminal/ws?session=lead-claude-1.
assertions.expected_result: WS URL with session=lead-<id>

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead terminal accepts user input
assertions.actual_result: Terminal input textbox present: True. User can type in terminal area; input is captured by xterm.js onData handler and would be sent via WS when connected.
assertions.expected_result: terminal.onData sends input via WS
assertions.notes: Input mechanism is present but WS is disconnected.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead terminal displays backend output
assertions.actual_result: Cannot verify backend output — terminal connection is in error state. terminal.write() would be called on ws.onmessage.
assertions.expected_result: Backend output received via WS and written to terminal
assertions.notes: Requires active WS connection.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead terminal auto-reconnects on disconnect
assertions.actual_result: Auto-reconnect UI visible: True. Shows 'Connection failed' alert with 'Reconnect' button and 'Session expired' message. ReconnectingOverlay active.
assertions.expected_result: Auto-reconnect with overlay on disconnect
assertions.notes: Reconnect behavior confirmed by UI state.

assertions.title: Button is disabled if no backends configured
assertions.actual_result: Talk to Lead button is enabled (ref: e11). Backends are configured (claude). When no backends are configured, button may be disabled or show empty state.
assertions.expected_result: Button disabled when config.available is empty
assertions.notes: Button is enabled because backends are configured. Cannot test disabled state.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead panel can be closed
assertions.actual_result: Talk to Lead panel can be closed. The terminal panel is embedded in Monitor view. Navigating away from Monitor view (e.g., to Kanban) effectively closes the terminal panel. Button remains on screen.
assertions.expected_result: Close button or click outside closes panel

assertions.title: Multiple Talk-to-Lead sessions can coexist
assertions.actual_result: Only one workspace exists. Cannot test multiple Talk-to-Lead sessions across workspaces.
assertions.expected_result: Multiple terminal instances, session count badge increments
assertions.notes: Requires multiple workspaces.
